definition: A charged particle formed when an atom, or a group of atoms, loses or gains electrons. Ions can carry a positive or a negative charge.
msAccepts: a charged particle formed by electron loss or gain
an atom or group of atoms with an overall charge
msAvoids: a particle that changes its protons

definition: A positive ion, formed when an atom loses electrons — for example Na⁺. All metal ions are cations.
msAccepts: a positively charged ion
formed by losing electrons
msAvoids: an ion that has gained protons

definition: A negative ion, formed when an atom gains electrons — for example Cl⁻.
msAccepts: a negatively charged ion
formed by gaining electrons
msAvoids: an ion that has lost electrons
an ion with more protons than electrons

definition: The attraction between positively and negatively charged particles — the force that holds oppositely charged ions together throughout an ionic lattice.
msAccepts: positive and negative charges attract
the attraction between oppositely charged ions
msAvoids: a force between ions of the same charge

definition: A diagram of ionic bonding showing outer-shell electrons only, with one atom's electrons as dots and the other's as crosses, and the charges on the ions shown.
msAccepts: outer electrons only
dots and crosses show which atom each electron came from
msAvoids: dots and crosses are different types of electron

definition: Having the same number of electrons: the sodium ion [2, 8] is isoelectronic with the neon atom [2, 8].
msAccepts: same number of electrons
same electronic configuration

definition: A regular, repeating array of particles; an ionic lattice packs positive and negative ions together in a repeating three-dimensional pattern.
msAccepts: a regular repeating arrangement of particles
repeating pattern of ions
msAvoids: a single unit of the compound

definition: A structure in which vast numbers of oppositely charged ions are held by electrostatic attraction extending in all directions; there are no individual molecules.
msAccepts: giant structure of oppositely charged ions
no individual molecules — attraction extends throughout
msAvoids: a lattice of atoms sharing electrons

definition: An ion made of more than one atom — for example NO₃⁻, CO₃²⁻, SO₄²⁻, OH⁻ and NH₄⁺. Brackets are written when a formula needs more than one of them.
msAccepts: an ion containing more than one atom
brackets needed when more than one appears in a formula
msAvoids: an ion that is always singly charged

definition: Melted — the solid has been heated until it is a liquid.
msAccepts: melted
in the liquid state after heating

definition: A substance dissolved in water; its state symbol is (aq).
msAccepts: dissolved in water
solution with water as the solvent
